content.comment_body: Hello, does anyone know how to record the time when an input is set high and display that time on the [product_name]'s LCD? I have one input for start time and another for stop time.
Are you familiar with the Stopwatch block in [product_name] Soft Comfort?
Yes, I've seen it before but haven't used it.
Would you like to see an example?
I need to log the exact time, such as 12:30am, when input I1 changes from low to high.

Sorry, I misunderstood earlier. You want to know exactly when input I1 switches from low (0) to high (1)? On the [product_name], there's no direct access to real date and time. You can only use message texts that can be acknowledged.
Thanks, that's working well. One more thing: can I use inputs I1 and I2 to pause or resume program execution?
No, if a [product_name] is running, you cannot stop the program externally via digital inputs. You can only do this through the device system menu or with [product_name] Soft Comfort.

While you can't truly start and stop the device, you can use set/reset functions on your logic, controlled by one or more inputs. The program keeps running, but you can prevent outputs from activating. That might cover your needs for now.

For my case, say I1 is Start Pump and I2 is Stop Pump. I want the LCD to show start and stop times like this: Start Time: 10:00 (when I1 went high) Stop Time: 11:00 (when I2 went high). The function to pause or resume the program is no longer necessary.

One way is to use separate message texts for start and stop times, so the date and time can appear when the messages are triggered. If you want both times shown on one screen, you can synchronize a stopwatch with a weekly timer at 12:00 PM, letting the stopwatch act as a day timer and display several times in one message. Keep in mind, on the first day the time could be inaccurate until 12:00 PM. See the attached example file.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are trying to capture and display the exact time when a digital input changes state on the [product_name]'s display. They found that it's not possible to directly access the real date and time in the system, only to use acknowledgeable messages. Direct control over program execution via inputs is limited, but outputs can be controlled using logical set/reset operations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to log and display event timestamps, and to control program start and stop actions via specified digital inputs.
